items.label: ASE Group Q2 FY2026 (07-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: LEAP (leading-edge advanced packaging) revenue is tracking ~USD 200M AHEAD

set.signal: LEAP (leading-edge advanced packaging) revenue is tracking ~USD 200M AHEAD of the USD 3.5B 2026 guidance and management is aiming to DOUBLE LEAP revenue in 2027. Full-process CoWoS-like packaging is on track for ~USD 300M in 2026 with substantial growth in 2027; CFO Joseph Tung: 'I think the full process will also be another margin accretive business for us'. ASE's fully automated PANEL line (310mm x 310mm) is to start production by Q1 2027, complementary to foundry CoWoS and serving the same customer set at a similar reticle size and pitch / line-width range. Capacity — not demand — is the constraint: blended utilization 80-85% but effectively full, with growth gated by equipment installation and building construction (13 greenfield plus 8 brownfield projects underway). FY2026 capex raised by another $2 billion to a total of 'about ... 10.5 billion' ($6.5 billion of it equipment), ~70% of equipment capex going to leading edge.

items.label: ASE Group Q2 FY2026 (07-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: GENERAL-MARKET OSAT OUTLOOK MORE THAN DOUBLED

set.signal: GENERAL-MARKET OSAT OUTLOOK RAISED (COO Dr. Tien Wu): the non-LEAP/general segment is now expected to grow 30% YoY in 2026 versus the previous guidance of 13%, with very strong demand in INDUSTRIAL, POWER, CONNECTIVITY and STORAGE devices; Dr. Wu believes ASE will outperform the general semiconductor market on its association with AI infrastructure and its fully automated lines. Non-LEAP capacity is tight — wire bond and traditional advanced packaging were tight in Q2 — and the assembly business has shown even stronger than expected growth, 'especially as it relates to legacy wire bond services', so management now believes assembly and test will grow at similar rates in 2026, versus the start-of-year view that wafer-sort-led test would outpace assembly. Blended utilization 80-85%, with capacities outside lines being placed into service generally very close to full; CFO Joseph Tung: ASE also needs to add capacity for mainstream advanced packaging and testing to support general market demand. Record ATM revenue NTD 126.1B (+36% YoY) with ATM gross margin 27.3%.
set.figure: general segment +30% YoY (was 13%); wire bond tight; assembly and test to grow at similar rates

items.reason: 'More than doubled' is a derived comparison, not stated; 'assembly growing at least as fast as test' overstates — IR said both 'will grow at similar rates'. Speakers attributed.
items.evidence: We now believe that both our assembly and test businesses will grow at similar rates during the year.

items.label: ASE Group Q2 FY2026 (07-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CAPEX RAISED BY USD 2B (another USD 1B each for facilities and equipment)

set.signal: CAPEX RAISED BY USD 2B (another USD 1B each for facilities and equipment), taking full-year 2026 capex to a total of 'about ... 10.5 billion' — CFO: '$4 billion is for factory and facilities, $6.5 billion for equipment'; the additional facilities and most of the equipment are for LEAP, with capacity also added for mainstream advanced packaging and testing. Equipment split: ~56% assembly, ~40% test, remainder EMS and materials; ~70% of equipment capex is for LEADING EDGE. Q2 alone: machinery capex USD 1.7B (USD 840M packaging, USD 804M testing, USD 49M EMS, USD 2M interconnect materials); H1 machinery USD 2.7B plus USD 1.4B buildings/automation. Construction is the pressure point: 13 GREENFIELD projects plus 8 BROWNFIELD projects (existing factories bought and renovated) running simultaneously — 'these 20 projects' — which CFO Joseph Tung thinks will be sufficient to carry ASE into 2028, 'maybe into some part of 2029'. CFO: very heavy capex this year and going into next year, and 'the negative cash flow situation will remain for some time'; on 2027 capex: 'I know it's going to be big, but how big?' — another quarter or so for better clarity.
set.figure: FY26 capex about 10.5 billion (+$2 billion): $6.5 billion equipment / $4 billion facilities; 70% of equipment = leading edge; 13 greenfield + 8 brownfield

items.reason: 'Quarterly capex now EXCEEDS EBITDA' was the analyst's (Charlie Chan) remark, not management's; '2027 capex will rise again' was the analyst's (Gokul Hariharan) framing — the CFO said only it is 'going to be big'; the CFO's hedges on 2028/2029 restored. Verifier: the 10.5 billion total is transcribed 'TWD 10.5 billion' (garbled; the parts are '$4 billion' / '$6.5 billion'), so no currency word is attached to the total.
items.evidence: I think we will continue to have very heavy CapEx for this year. Not only this year, but also going into next year. I think the negative cash flow situation will remain for some time.

items.label: ASE Group Q2 FY2026 (07-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Technology roadmap. PANEL: ASE's fully automated panel line

set.signal: Technology roadmap. PANEL: ASE's fully automated panel line will start PRODUCTION BY Q1 2027 in a 310mm x 310mm form factor — COO Dr. Tien Wu: 'quite complementary' to foundry CoWoS, 'actually the same customer set', a similar reticle size, and pitch / line width covering the similar range; which customer adopts what depends on capacity, performance and speed of execution. GLASS SUBSTRATE: NOT in production and not for the next 12 months; R&D is evaluating feasibility and economics with the substrate supplier, the foundry and customers. FULL-PROCESS (CoWoS-like): on track for about USD 300M of revenue in 2026 with aggressive capacity expansion and substantial growth in 2027; margin not yet fully reflected, and CFO Joseph Tung thinks it will be margin-accretive. CPO: Dr. Wu: 'towards the end of the year, the CPO will start launching. Initially, could be in small volume', yielding critical benchmark information on bandwidth, system performance and thermal dissipation; more detail on CPO services, revenue and the 2027 outlook in two quarters. Bigger reticle sizes drive panel / more-complex CoWoS first; as optics come in, POWER DELIVERY becomes the next question, to be deployed in the next two to three years.
set.figure: panel 310x310mm production by Q1 2027; glass substrate not within 12 months; full-process ~USD 300M 2026; CPO starts launching toward end-2026

items.reason: Dr. Wu said the reticle size is 'similar' (not identical) and that CPO 'could be in small volume' initially — hedges restored and speakers attributed.
items.evidence: They're quite complementary. It's actually the same customer set. Similar, the reticle size. In terms of the pitch size line width, they're all identical, cover the similar range.

items.label: ASE Group Q2 FY2026 (07-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Service-mix and competitive positioning. ASSEMBLY IS NOW KEEPING PACE WITH TEST

set.signal: Service-mix and competitive positioning. ASSEMBLY IS NOW KEEPING PACE WITH TEST: entering the year management expected test (led by rapid wafer-sort expansion) to outgrow assembly, but assembly has grown even more strongly than expected — 'especially as it relates to legacy wire bond services' — so both are now expected to grow at similar rates in 2026, and CFO Joseph Tung expects the 2027 LEAP mix to be 'pretty much similar' to this year's. Computing applications keep rising as a share of ATM revenue, a trend management sees continuing into 2027 and 2028. On EMIB as a CoWoS alternative, COO Dr. Tien Wu is deliberately agnostic: as a PURE-PLAY OSAT, 'we have no conflict with foundry, with no conflict with substrate provider'; 'If the EMIB substrate becomes the right alternative, we'll just buy EMIB substrate and we do the assembly' — not a zero-sum threat. U.S. footprint: test development and services in California with factories in Fremont and San Jose, extending to a third and fourth factory; but manufacturing PROCESS development stays in Taiwan until scale and efficiency are proven, then, in due time, migrates with customers.
set.figure: assembly now matching test growth (legacy wire bond strong); EMIB treated as pure-play-neutral

items.reason: Quote 'no conflict with foundry, no conflict with substrate provider' was not verbatim; the 2027 mix statement is the CFO's hedged view; speakers attributed.
items.evidence: In future, this could be one of the competitive advantage for ASE as a pure-play OSAT, that we have no conflict with foundry, with no conflict with substrate provider.
